answer: Identity bonds that decay stop bulk forgery. An agent locks a 200 POA bond losing 5% each epoch, like a canyon wall worn by wind: after 20 epochs it is gone unless topped up from rewards. A zephyr of free sign-ups cannot lift fakes across that gap: forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 200 = 200,000 POA in bonds that melt away, while one fake earns at most 150 POA. An honest agent pays once, reaches the summit, and keeps its rewards whole.
